Cellular angiofibroma of the lower femal.normalized_text: Cellular angiofibroma of the lower female genital tract
Cellular angiofibroma of the lower femal.description: A rare benign mesenchymal tumor, usually arising in the vulvovaginal or paravaginal region. It is typically small, well circumscribed, composed of bland spindle cells, collagenous stroma, and numerous hyalinized vessels.

Mammary-type myofibroblastoma.description: A benign spindle-cell neoplasm that can occur along the embryonic milk line, including the vulvovaginal and inguinal regions. It is usually circumscribed and contains myofibroblasts, abundant hyalinized collagen, and variable thin-walled vessels.

Angiomyofibroblastoma.description: A benign mesenchymal tumor of the vulva or vagina, generally small and circumscribed. Histologically it contains stromal spindle or epithelioid cells concentrated around numerous blood vessels.

Aggressive angiomyxoma.description: A locally infiltrative mesenchymal tumor usually occurring in the pelvis, perineum, or vulvovaginal region of women. It is characterized by myxoid stroma and numerous vessels and may recur after excision.

Leiomyoma (including vaginal or cervical.description: A benign smooth-muscle tumor that may arise from the uterus, cervix, or rarely the vagina. Leiomyomas are commonly well circumscribed and often demonstrate low T2 signal because of smooth muscle and fibrous tissue.

Acute pyelonephritis (focal or multifoca.normalized_text: Acute pyelonephritis (focal or multifocal bacterial nephritis)
Acute pyelonephritis (focal or multifoca.description: Bacterial infection of the renal parenchyma that can produce focal wedge-shaped areas of edema, altered echogenicity, reduced perfusion, and heterogeneous signal on MRI.

Acute focal bacterial nephritis (acute l.normalized_text: Acute focal bacterial nephritis (acute lobar nephronia)
Acute focal bacterial nephritis (acute l.description: A localized severe form of renal infection, intermediate between uncomplicated pyelonephritis and renal abscess, causing a poorly defined focal inflammatory renal mass without a drainable fluid collection.

Renal infarction.description: Ischemic necrosis of renal tissue caused by interruption of arterial blood supply, typically producing peripheral wedge-shaped lesions with reduced or absent perfusion.

Renal abscess.description: A localized collection of pus within the kidney, often developing as a complication of pyelonephritis or hematogenous infection; imaging may show a focal heterogeneous lesion with peripheral vascularity.

Renal neoplasm, such as renal cell carci.normalized_text: Renal neoplasm, such as renal cell carcinoma
Renal neoplasm, such as renal cell carci.description: A primary renal tumor that may appear as a focal heterogeneous renal mass with internal vascularity and variable MRI signal characteristics.

Hepatocellular carcinoma with portal vei.normalized_text: Hepatocellular carcinoma with portal vein tumor thrombus
Hepatocellular carcinoma with portal vei.description: Primary liver cancer arising from hepatocytes, often presenting as a large heterogeneous hepatic mass and capable of invading the portal venous system.

Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.description: A primary malignancy of intrahepatic bile ducts that can appear as a large infiltrative hepatic mass, sometimes with vascular encasement or invasion.

Hepatic metastasis.description: Secondary malignant deposits in the liver from an extrahepatic primary cancer; metastases may be solitary or multifocal and can become large and necrotic.

Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON).description: A mitochondrial inherited optic neuropathy causing sequential or bilateral central visual loss, optic-disc vascular changes in early stages, and later optic atrophy with retinal nerve fiber layer loss.

Autosomal dominant optic atrophy (DOA, c.normalized_text: Autosomal dominant optic atrophy (DOA, commonly OPA1-related)
Autosomal dominant optic atrophy (DOA, c.description: An inherited optic neuropathy characterized by slowly progressive bilateral optic atrophy, usually with temporal disc pallor, reduced color vision, central visual-field defects, and diffuse or temporal retinal nerve fiber layer thinning.

Chronic bilateral optic neuritis or demy.normalized_text: Chronic bilateral optic neuritis or demyelinating optic neuropathy
Chronic bilateral optic neuritis or demy.description: Inflammatory or demyelinating injury to the optic nerves can result in optic disc pallor and persistent retinal nerve fiber layer thinning after one or more episodes of optic neuritis; causes include multiple sclerosis, MOG-antibody disease, and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.

Glaucomatous optic neuropathy.description: A chronic progressive optic neuropathy, usually associated with elevated or susceptible intraocular pressure, producing retinal nerve fiber layer loss and characteristic optic-disc cupping with visual-field defects.

Wilson disease (hepatolenticular degener.description: An autosomal-recessive disorder of impaired copper transport caused by pathogenic ATP7B variants, leading to copper accumulation in the liver, cornea, and brain, particularly the basal ganglia.

Acquired hepatocerebral degeneration due.normalized_text: Acquired hepatocerebral degeneration due to chronic liver disease
Acquired hepatocerebral degeneration due.description: A neurologic syndrome associated with chronic liver failure or portosystemic shunting, often causing manganese deposition in the basal ganglia and resulting in characteristic T1 MRI hyperintensity with movement and cognitive symptoms.

Manganese neurotoxicity (manganism).description: A toxic movement-disorder syndrome caused by chronic manganese exposure or impaired biliary manganese excretion; it commonly affects the globus pallidus and produces T1 hyperintensity on brain MRI.

Olecranon bursitis.description: Inflammation and fluid accumulation in the bursa over the tip of the elbow (olecranon), often caused by pressure, repetitive trauma, or injury.

Septic olecranon bursitis.description: Infection of the olecranon bursa, commonly caused by bacteria entering through a skin break, abrasion, or puncture near the elbow.

Cellulitis of the elbow region.description: A bacterial infection of the skin and subcutaneous tissues that causes expanding redness, warmth, swelling, and tenderness.

Traumatic olecranon bursitis or elbow co.normalized_text: Traumatic olecranon bursitis or elbow contusion
Traumatic olecranon bursitis or elbow co.description: Swelling and bruising after direct impact or repetitive pressure on the elbow, which may cause bleeding or fluid accumulation in the olecranon bursa.

Adenoid hypertrophy.description: Enlargement of nasopharyngeal lymphoid tissue (adenoids), which can narrow the nasopharyngeal airway and contribute to upper-airway obstruction.

Obstructive sleep apnea due to upper-air.normalized_text: Obstructive sleep apnea due to upper-airway soft-tissue crowding
Obstructive sleep apnea due to upper-air.description: Sleep-related recurrent upper-airway obstruction that may be associated with enlarged adenoids, tonsils, tongue base, or other pharyngeal soft tissues.

Retropharyngeal edema or retropharyngeal.description: Inflammation or infection in the retropharyngeal space that can cause prevertebral soft-tissue thickening and potentially compromise the airway; an abscess generally shows a drainable fluid collection, often with rim enhancement on contrast imaging.

Insulinoma.description: A pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor that secretes insulin autonomously, causing endogenous hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia.

Sulfonylurea- or meglitinide-induced hyp.description: Hypoglycemia caused by insulin secretagogue medications, which stimulate pancreatic insulin release and therefore produce high insulin and high C-peptide levels.

Non-insulinoma pancreatogenous hypoglyce.description: Diffuse pancreatic beta-cell hyperfunction causing excessive endogenous insulin secretion, often resulting in recurrent hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia.

Insulin autoimmune syndrome (Hirata dise.description: A rare cause of spontaneous hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia caused by insulin autoantibodies that bind and later release insulin.

Congenital rib synostosis (fused ribs).description: A congenital chest-wall anomaly in which adjacent ribs are partially or completely joined by bone or cartilage. It may be isolated or associated with vertebral segmentation abnormalities.

Congenital bifid rib (forked rib).description: A developmental rib anomaly in which a rib divides into two branches, most often anteriorly. It is usually asymptomatic and may be found incidentally on imaging.

Healed rib fracture with callus formatio.normalized_text: Healed rib fracture with callus formation
Healed rib fracture with callus formatio.description: Prior rib trauma can heal with irregular bony callus, cortical thickening, deformity, or bridging between adjacent ribs. Imaging correlation with radiographs or CT is generally needed.

Pneumatosis cystoides intestinalis.description: A benign or secondary condition characterized by multiple gas-filled cysts within the submucosa or subserosa of the intestinal wall, often involving the colon. Endoscopy may show smooth, cystic, polyp-like submucosal lesions, and histology can show empty cystic spaces with foreign-body giant cell reaction.

Colonic lymphangiomatosis (multiple colo.description: A rare benign lymphatic malformation that can produce multiple submucosal cystic lesions in the colon. Lesions contain lymphatic fluid rather than gas and may resemble cystic polyps endoscopically.

Colonic lipomatosis or multiple colonic.normalized_text: Colonic lipomatosis or multiple colonic lipomas
Colonic lipomatosis or multiple colonic.description: Benign fatty tumors or diffuse fatty infiltration of the colonic submucosa that can create smooth, rounded submucosal bulges during colonoscopy.

Leucemia eosinofílica crónica, no especi.normalized_text: Leucemia eosinofílica crónica, no especificada de otra manera (CEL-NOS)
Leucemia eosinofílica crónica, no especi.description: Una neoplasia mieloide clonal caracterizada por hipereosinofilia persistente, maduración anormal de eosinófilos, citopenias y/o hematopoyeesis displásica, a menudo con anomalías citogenéticas tras la exclusión de neoplasias eosinofílicas definidas por reordenamiento específico.

Síndrome mielodisplásico/neoplasia mielo.description: Una neoplasia mieloide solapada en la que la producción ineficaz y displásica de células sanguíneas coexiste con características proliferativas como la eosinofilia; pueden estar presentes anomalías cromosómicas y células displásicas.

Neoplasia mieloide/linfoide con eosinofi.normalized_text: Neoplasia mieloide/linfoide con eosinofilia y reorganización del gen tirosina quinasa
Neoplasia mieloide/linfoide con eosinofi.description: Un grupo de neoplasias hematológicas clonales impulsadas por reordenamientos que involucran genes como PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1 o PCM1-JAK2. Comúnmente causan eosinofilia marcada y pueden producir anemia y maduración mieloide anormal.

Síndrome idiopático hipereosinofílico (H.description: Un diagnóstico de exclusión definido por hipereosinofilia persistente, generalmente con daño orgánico asociado a eosinófilos, tras excluir causas secundarias y clonales.

diagnoses.name: Mixed-cellularity subtype of classic Hodgkin's lymphoma
diagnoses.normalized_text: Mixed-cellularity subtype of classic Hodgkin's lymphoma

Multisystem Langerhans cell histiocytosi.description: A clonal histiocytic neoplasm characterized by proliferation of Langerhans cells, often showing grooved nuclei and immunoreactivity for CD1a, langerin/CD207, and S100. It can involve lymph nodes, bone, skin, lungs, liver, spleen, kidneys, and the gastrointestinal or genitourinary tract.

Rosai-Dorfman disease.description: A non-Langerhans histiocytic disorder causing painless lymph-node enlargement and sometimes extranodal disease involving the skin, upper respiratory tract, kidneys, or retroperitoneum. Histology typically shows large S100-positive histiocytes with emperipolesis.

Systemic lymphoma, including non-Hodgkin.description: Lymphoma is a malignant proliferation of lymphoid cells that can present with widespread lymphadenopathy and extranodal abdominal involvement, including renal, retroperitoneal, bowel, and pelvic disease.

Erdheim-Chester disease.description: A rare non-Langerhans histiocytic neoplasm, usually driven by MAPK-pathway mutations, that can involve retroperitoneal tissue, kidneys, cardiovascular structures, bones, and the central nervous system. Histology generally shows foamy CD68-positive, CD1a-negative histiocytes.

Malaria severa por Plasmodium falciparum.description: Una malaria potencialmente mortal causada por Plasmodium falciparum, caracterizada por alta parásitemia, hemólisis, trombocitopenia y posible disfunción renal y hepática. Las imágenes de la citología muestran formas intraeritrocíticas del anillo compatibles con la malaria, y el patrón de prueba rápida es compatible con la infección por P. falciparum.

Infección mixta por malaria (Plasmodium.normalized_text: Infección mixta por malaria (Plasmodium falciparum con otra especie de Plasmodium)
Infección mixta por malaria (Plasmodium.description: Infección concurrente con P. falciparum y otra especie de malaria, como P. vivax, P. malariae o P. ovale. Algunos patrones de pruebas rápidas de malaria pueden sugerir P. falciparum o infección mixta, aunque se requiere identificación microscópica y/o PCR para confirmar.

Babesiosis.description: Una infección protozoaria intraeritrocítica transmitida por garrapatas que puede causar anemia hemolítica, trombocitopenia, disfunción hepática y lesión renal. Puede parecerse a la malaria en un frotis sanguíneo, pero Babesia suele mostrar tétradas (formas cruzadas de Malta) y no produciría un resultado específico de prueba rápida para malaria.

Esophageal perforation with mediastiniti.description: A full-thickness tear or hole in the esophageal wall causing leakage of saliva, contrast, and gastrointestinal contents into the mediastinum, resulting in mediastinal infection and pus formation.

Boerhaave syndrome (spontaneous esophage.description: A spontaneous transmural esophageal rupture, classically occurring after forceful vomiting or retching, which can rapidly cause mediastinitis and sepsis.

Iatrogenic esophageal perforation.description: An esophageal wall injury caused by medical instrumentation, such as endoscopy, dilation, transesophageal echocardiography, surgery, or foreign-body removal, with subsequent mediastinal leakage and infection.

Esophageal foreign-body perforation.description: Perforation of the esophagus caused by an impacted foreign body, commonly a fish bone, denture, or sharp object, potentially causing localized mediastinal abscess formation.

Large left pleural effusion with compres.normalized_text: Large left pleural effusion with compressive atelectasis
Large left pleural effusion with compres.description: Accumulation of fluid in the left pleural space causing partial collapse/compression of the adjacent left lower lung. A smaller right pleural effusion may also be present.

Malignant pleural effusion.description: Pleural fluid caused by metastatic cancer or a primary pleural/lung malignancy; it is often unilateral, large, recurrent, and can produce compressive atelectasis.

Congestive heart failure with bilateral.normalized_text: Congestive heart failure with bilateral pleural effusions
Congestive heart failure with bilateral.description: Cardiac failure can raise hydrostatic pressure in the pulmonary circulation and cause pleural effusions, commonly bilateral but sometimes markedly asymmetric.

Parapneumonic pleural effusion or empyem.description: Pleural fluid occurring secondary to pneumonia; infected pleural fluid is termed empyema and may be associated with adjacent consolidation or atelectasis.

Chylothorax.description: Accumulation of lymphatic fluid in the pleural space, commonly due to thoracic duct obstruction or injury, lymphoma, mediastinal malignancy, or postoperative trauma. It can be unilateral or bilateral and may become large.

Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD).description: A rapidly progressive prion-mediated neurodegenerative disease. EEG may show periodic sharp-wave complexes, often generalized, biphasic or triphasic, recurring about once per second.

Toxic-metabolic encephalopathy with trip.description: Diffuse cerebral dysfunction caused by metabolic or toxic disturbances, commonly hepatic failure, uremia, severe systemic illness, or medication effects. EEG often shows generalized periodic discharges with triphasic morphology and diffuse slowing.

Nonconvulsive status epilepticus (NCSE).description: Persistent or recurrent electrographic seizure activity without prominent convulsive movements. Generalized periodic discharges can lie on the ictal-interictal continuum and may represent NCSE depending on frequency, evolution, clinical correlation, and response to antiseizure treatment.

Obturator hernia with small-bowel obstru.description: A rare pelvic hernia in which bowel protrudes through the obturator canal, typically between the pectineus and obturator muscles. It may cause incarceration and bowel obstruction.

Incarcerated obturator hernia.description: An obturator hernia in which the herniated bowel is trapped and cannot be reduced, creating risk for bowel obstruction, strangulation, and ischemia.

Femoral hernia with bowel involvement.description: A groin hernia in which bowel protrudes through the femoral canal below the inguinal ligament. Femoral hernias can become incarcerated and cause bowel obstruction, although the depicted location is more characteristic of an obturator hernia.

Susac syndrome.description: A rare autoimmune microangiopathy affecting the brain, retina, and inner ear, classically causing encephalopathy/corpus callosum lesions, branch retinal artery occlusions, and sensorineural hearing loss.

Multiple sclerosis.description: An immune-mediated demyelinating disease of the central nervous system that can produce white-matter and corpus callosum lesions and diverse neurologic visual symptoms.

Primary angiitis of the central nervous.normalized_text: Primary angiitis of the central nervous system or systemic retinal vasculitis
Primary angiitis of the central nervous.description: Inflammatory vasculitic disorders can damage small and medium vessels in the retina and brain, resulting in retinal ischemia and ischemic brain lesions.

Cogan syndrome.description: A rare inflammatory disorder characterized by ocular inflammation and audiovestibular dysfunction, often with sensorineural hearing loss; systemic vasculitis may occur.

Myoclonic epilepsy with ragged-red fiber.normalized_text: Myoclonic epilepsy with ragged-red fibers (MERRF syndrome)
Myoclonic epilepsy with ragged-red fiber.description: A maternally inherited mitochondrial disorder, most often caused by an MT-TK mitochondrial DNA mutation, characterized by myoclonic epilepsy, mitochondrial myopathy, elevated CK, and ragged-red fibers on muscle biopsy.

Mitochondrial myopathy due to a mitochon.normalized_text: Mitochondrial myopathy due to a mitochondrial DNA mutation
Mitochondrial myopathy due to a mitochon.description: A group of disorders caused by impaired mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation. They can produce proximal or axial muscle weakness, camptocormia, elevated CK, seizures, brain abnormalities, and characteristic ragged-red/oxidative-enzyme-deficient muscle fibers.

MELAS syndrome (mitochondrial encephalom.normalized_text: MELAS syndrome (mitochondrial encephalomyopathy, lactic acidosis, and stroke-like episodes)
MELAS syndrome (mitochondrial encephalom.description: A mitochondrial DNA disorder, commonly related to the m.3243A>G variant, causing maternally inherited encephalomyopathy, seizures, myopathy, and mitochondrial abnormalities on muscle biopsy.

Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy associat.normalized_text: Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy associated with the m.8344A>G MT-TK mutation
Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy associat.description: A mitochondrial tRNA-lysine mutation classically associated with MERRF but capable of causing variable phenotypes including isolated mitochondrial myopathy, camptocormia, epilepsy, and respiratory-chain-deficient fibers.

diagnoses.normalized_text: B-cell lymphoma, unclassifiable, with features intermediate between diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and Burkitt lymphoma

Acute megakaryoblastic leukemia (AMKL; A.normalized_text: Acute megakaryoblastic leukemia (AMKL; AML with megakaryocytic differentiation)
Acute megakaryoblastic leukemia (AMKL; A.description: A subtype of acute myeloid leukemia composed of immature megakaryoblasts, often showing cytoplasmic blebbing and platelet-lineage marker expression. It may be associated with complex chromosomal abnormalities or recurrent fusion genes.

Acute myeloid leukemia with myelodysplas.normalized_text: Acute myeloid leukemia with myelodysplasia-related changes (AML-MR)
Acute myeloid leukemia with myelodysplas.description: An acute myeloid leukemia associated with myelodysplasia-related cytogenetic abnormalities, prior myelodysplastic syndrome, or characteristic myeloid gene mutations. Complex karyotypes are common and generally indicate high-risk disease.

Acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoblast.description: A malignant proliferation of immature B- or T-lymphoid precursors that can involve bone marrow, blood, lymph nodes, or extranodal tissues. Cytogenetic abnormalities may be present, although lineage-specific immunophenotyping is required for confirmation.

Hepatic peliosis.description: A rare benign vascular liver condition characterized by multiple blood-filled cystic spaces within the hepatic parenchyma; it may be associated with medications, malignancy, chronic illness, or anabolic steroid exposure.

Hepatic hemangiomatosis or multiple hepa.normalized_text: Hepatic hemangiomatosis or multiple hepatic hemangiomas
Hepatic hemangiomatosis or multiple hepa.description: Hemangiomas are benign vascular tumors of the liver. Multiple lesions may produce a heterogeneous liver appearance and can vary in echogenicity and enhancement depending on imaging phase.

Hepatic metastases.description: Metastatic liver disease occurs when a malignancy from another primary site spreads to the liver and commonly presents as multiple focal liver lesions.

Hepatic lymphoma.description: Primary or secondary hepatic lymphoma can produce multiple hypodense liver nodules, diffuse hepatic infiltration, hepatomegaly, and sometimes splenic involvement.

Hepatosplenic candidiasis or other disse.normalized_text: Hepatosplenic candidiasis or other disseminated fungal microabscesses
Hepatosplenic candidiasis or other disse.description: Disseminated fungal infection, especially candidiasis in immunocompromised patients, may cause multiple small hepatic and splenic microabscesses that appear as hypoechoic or hypodense lesions.

Hyperkalemia.description: Elevated serum potassium causing characteristic ECG changes, initially including tall, narrow, symmetric peaked T waves and shortened repolarization; more severe cases cause PR prolongation, QRS widening, and sine-wave morphology.

Acute anterior myocardial infarction wit.normalized_text: Acute anterior myocardial infarction with hyperacute T waves
Acute anterior myocardial infarction wit.description: Acute occlusion of the left anterior descending coronary artery may initially produce localized broad, prominent hyperacute T waves in anterior chest leads before classic ST-segment elevation develops.

De Winter ECG pattern due to proximal le.normalized_text: De Winter ECG pattern due to proximal left anterior descending artery occlusion
De Winter ECG pattern due to proximal le.description: A STEMI-equivalent pattern associated with acute proximal LAD occlusion, characterized by upsloping ST depression at the J point in the anterior leads followed by tall symmetric T waves, often with slight ST elevation in aVR.

Benign early repolarization pattern.description: A nonischemic ECG variant, often seen in younger healthy individuals, with concave ST elevation, J-point notching or slurring, and relatively prominent T waves in precordial leads.

Congenital lobar emphysema (congenital l.description: A neonatal congenital lung malformation in which a pulmonary lobe becomes progressively overinflated due to partial bronchial obstruction or abnormal bronchial cartilage, causing compression of adjacent lung and possible mediastinal shift.

Bronchopulmonary sequestration, likely i.description: A congenital nonfunctioning segment of lung that lacks normal bronchial communication and receives anomalous systemic arterial supply, commonly from the descending thoracic or abdominal aorta. It usually involves a lower lobe.

Congenital diaphragmatic hernia.description: A developmental defect of the diaphragm that allows abdominal organs to enter the thorax, most often posterolaterally on the left, producing lung compression and respiratory compromise in neonates.

Congenital pulmonary airway malformation.description: A congenital malformation of the lower respiratory tract characterized by cystic or solid abnormal lung tissue, often detected in newborns and commonly involving a single lobe. It may coexist with sequestration as a hybrid lesion.

Malignant hypertension with hyperplastic.description: Severe, rapidly progressive hypertension can cause concentric smooth-muscle and intimal thickening of small arteries and arterioles, producing an 'onion-skin' appearance and marked luminal narrowing; fibrinoid vascular injury may also occur.

Scleroderma renal crisis.description: A life-threatening complication of systemic sclerosis characterized by abrupt severe hypertension and renal thrombotic microangiopathy, often with hyperplastic ('onion-skin') arteriolosclerosis of renal vessels.

Renal thrombotic microangiopathy.description: Thrombotic microangiopathy is an endothelial-injury syndrome affecting arterioles and capillaries, causing vascular narrowing, thrombosis, intimal swelling or proliferation, and possible ischemic kidney damage. It may occur with malignant hypertension, complement-mediated disease, autoimmune disease, drugs, or transplantation.

Chronic hypertensive nephrosclerosis.description: Long-standing hypertension causes progressive renal arteriolar and arterial sclerosis, including wall thickening and luminal narrowing. In more severe cases it can overlap with hyperplastic arteriolosclerosis.

Chiari I malformation.description: A structural hindbrain abnormality in which the cerebellar tonsils descend below the foramen magnum, potentially crowding the cervicomedullary junction and impairing cerebrospinal fluid flow.

Basilar invagination (basilar impression.description: An upward displacement of the upper cervical spine, especially the odontoid process, toward the skull base that can cause ventral compression of the lower brainstem and upper spinal cord.

Retroflexed odontoid with ventral brains.normalized_text: Retroflexed odontoid with ventral brainstem compression
Retroflexed odontoid with ventral brains.description: A posteriorly angled odontoid process can encroach on the ventral surface of the cervicomedullary junction; it may occur with Chiari malformation, basilar invagination, or other craniovertebral junction abnormalities.

Atlantoaxial instability.description: Excessive movement or abnormal alignment between the atlas (C1) and axis (C2), sometimes related to ligamentous insufficiency, congenital abnormalities, inflammatory disease, or trauma; it can compromise the spinal cord or lower brainstem.

Leukonostok bilan bog'liq infeksion endo.description: Leuconostoc turlari tomonidan yuzaga keladigan infeksion endokardit, o'ziga xos vankomistinga chidamli gram-musbat kokklar bo'lib, vayronkor valvulyar infeksiya va katta o'simliklarni keltirib chiqarishi mumkin.

Mahalliy klapanli infeksion endokardit.description: Endokardial yuzadagi mikrob infektsiyasi, odatda yurak klapanini o'z ichiga oladi, bu o'simliklar, yallig'lanish, klapan buzilishi va ehtimoliy qaytish yoki yurak yetishmovchiligi bilan tavsiflanadi.

Vankomisingga chidamli gram-musbat kokka.normalized_text: Vankomisingga chidamli gram-musbat kokkal infeksion endokardit
Vankomisingga chidamli gram-musbat kokka.description: Yuqori darajadagi vankomistsin rezistentligiga ega gram-musbat organizm tomonidan yuzaga keladigan endokardit, masalan, Leuconostoc, Pediococcus, Lactobacillus yoki vancomyganga chidamli enterokokk; bu sabablarni aniqlash uchun organizmni aniqlash zarur.

Acute pulmonary embolism.description: Obstruction of a pulmonary artery by thrombus, typically originating from deep venous thrombosis. The CT image shows a contrast filling defect within a left pulmonary arterial branch, which is characteristic of pulmonary embolism.

Chronic pulmonary thromboembolism.description: Persistent or organized thrombus within pulmonary arteries following prior embolic events; it can lead to chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension.

Pulmonary artery tumor embolus or intrav.normalized_text: Pulmonary artery tumor embolus or intravascular metastasis
Pulmonary artery tumor embolus or intrav.description: Rare obstruction of pulmonary arteries by tumor material, usually in a patient with an underlying malignancy. It may mimic thromboembolic disease on CT.

Herpes simplex virus encephalitis.description: Acute necrotizing viral encephalitis, most commonly caused by HSV-1, with predilection for the medial and inferior temporal lobes, insulae, and orbitofrontal regions.

Autoimmune limbic encephalitis.description: Immune-mediated inflammation of the limbic system, often associated with antibodies such as LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B receptor, NMDA receptor, or paraneoplastic antibodies.

HHV-6 encephalitis.description: Viral limbic encephalitis caused by human herpesvirus-6, classically occurring in immunocompromised patients, particularly after hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation.

Paraneoplastic limbic encephalitis.description: A subtype of autoimmune limbic encephalitis caused by an immune response associated with an underlying malignancy, commonly small-cell lung cancer, testicular tumors, breast cancer, thymoma, or ovarian tumors.

Neumonía grave por Legionella (enfermeda.normalized_text: Neumonía grave por Legionella (enfermedad del legionario)
Neumonía grave por Legionella (enfermeda.description: Una neumonía bacteriana atípica grave causada por especies de Legionella, a menudo asociada con hiponatremia, elevación de enzimas hepáticas, elevación de creatina quinasa, inflamación sistémica e insuficiencia respiratoria.

Neumonía bacteriana grave con sepsis e i.normalized_text: Neumonía bacteriana grave con sepsis e insuficiencia respiratoria aguda
Neumonía bacteriana grave con sepsis e i.description: Una infección bacteriana pulmonar grave puede causar leucocitosis neutrofílica, inflamación sistémica, disfunción orgánica relacionada con la sepsis, profundas anomalías en el intercambio de gases y lesiones en el miocardio o los músculos esqueléticos.

Linfo-ostiocitosis hemofagocítica (HLH).normalized_text: Linfo-ostiocitosis hemofagocítica (HLH) o síndrome de activación de macrófagos
Linfo-ostiocitosis hemofagocítica (HLH).description: La HLH es un síndrome hiperinflamatorio potencialmente mortal caracterizado por una activación inmunitaria excesiva, ferritina alta, receptor soluble IL-2 elevado, disfunción hepática, citopenias o leucocitosis ocasionalmente temprana, y fallo multiorgánico.

Insuficiencia suprarrenal aguda (crisis.description: La crisis suprarrenal se debe a una producción insuficiente de cortisol y, a menudo, de aldosterona, causando hiponatremia, hiperkalemia, hipotensión o shock, hipoglucemia o, ocasionalmente, hiperglucemia por estrés, y deterioro sistémico severo.

Rabdomiólisis con anomalías metabólicas.normalized_text: Rabdomiólisis con anomalías metabólicas secundarias y lesión miocárdica
Rabdomiólisis con anomalías metabólicas.description: La rabdomiólisis es la descomposición del músculo esquelético que causa elevación de la creatina quinasa, hiperpotalemia, elevación de la transaminasa y posible lesión renal; puede ocurrir durante infecciones graves, hipoxia, inmovilización prolongada o enfermedad inflamatoria.

Tumorframkallað osteomalasi (onkogenisk.description: Ein keypt paraneoplastisk sjúka, sum er orsakað av einum vanliga lítlum FGF23-seytandi tumori, sum førir til nýrnafosfatminking, hypofosfatemi, skerda beinmineralisering og hægri alkaliska fosfatasa. Skurðviðgerð av tumorinum normaliserar vanliga FGF23 og fosfatstøði.

Fosfaturiskt mesenkymalt æxli (PMT).description: Ein sjáldsamur mesenkymal nývøkstur, sum vanliga framleiðir FGF23 og er tann vanligasti tumorurin, sum er ábyrgdur fyri tumorframkallaðum osteomalasi. Hesir tumorar kunnu koma fram í beini ella mjúkum vefjum, eisini í grindini.

X-bundin hypofosfatemi (XLH).description: Ein arvaligur FGF23-miðlaður nýrafosfat-minkandi sjúka, sum er orsakað av PHEX-genvariantum. Hon framleiðir kroniska hypofosfatemi, osteomalaci ella raket, og hægri alkalisk fosfatasa.

Autosomalt dominant hypofosfatemiskur ra.description: Ein arvaligur FGF23-miðlaður fosfatminkandi sjúka, sum er orsakað av variantum, ið minka niðurbrot av FGF23. Hon kann vísa seg í barna- ella vaksnamannalívinum við hypofosfatemi og osteomalasi.

Primær hyperparathyroidismi.description: Ein sjúka við ovurhonds útskiljing av parathyroid hormoni, vanliga frá parathyroid adenoma, sum elvir til hypercalcemia, økt beinskifti og tap av nýrafosfati.

Left-sided infective endocarditis with s.normalized_text: Left-sided infective endocarditis with systemic embolization
Left-sided infective endocarditis with s.description: Infection of a cardiac valve, often the aortic or mitral valve, producing a mobile vegetation that can cause valve destruction/regurgitation and emboli to the brain, spleen, kidneys, or other organs.

Cardioembolic acute ischemic stroke.description: An ischemic stroke caused by embolic occlusion of a cerebral artery, commonly originating from a cardiac source such as infective endocarditis, atrial fibrillation, mural thrombus, or a prosthetic valve.

Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis.description: Sterile platelet-fibrin vegetations on cardiac valves, usually associated with malignancy, autoimmune disease, or hypercoagulable states; these vegetations can embolize systemically.

Valvular cardiac tumor or thrombus with.normalized_text: Valvular cardiac tumor or thrombus with systemic emboli
Valvular cardiac tumor or thrombus with.description: A cardiac thrombus or less commonly a benign valvular tumor, such as papillary fibroelastoma, can appear as an echogenic mobile valvular mass and cause embolic stroke or other systemic infarcts.

Short-rib thoracic dysplasia 9 with or w.normalized_text: Short-rib thoracic dysplasia 9 with or without polydactyly (IFT140-related ciliopathy)
Short-rib thoracic dysplasia 9 with or w.description: An autosomal-recessive skeletal ciliopathy caused by biallelic IFT140 variants. It can cause short ribs and narrow thorax, rhizomelic limb shortening, epiphyseal abnormalities, brachydactyly, renal disease progressing to renal failure, and ocular abnormalities.

Cranioectodermal dysplasia (Sensenbrenne.description: A rare autosomal-recessive ciliopathy characterized by craniosynostosis or dolichocephaly, ectodermal abnormalities involving hair, teeth and nails, skeletal dysplasia with a narrow thorax and short limbs, kidney disease, and occasional retinal or other ocular involvement.

Mainzer-Saldino syndrome.description: A skeletal-renal ciliopathy featuring cone-rod retinal dystrophy or other ocular disease, chronic kidney disease, phalangeal cone-shaped epiphyses, and mild-to-moderate short-rib skeletal dysplasia. IFT140 is among the genes associated with this phenotype.

Jeune syndrome / asphyxiating thoracic d.description: A genetically heterogeneous short-rib thoracic dysplasia and ciliopathy characterized by a narrow thorax, short ribs, respiratory complications, limb shortening, brachydactyly, and variable renal, hepatic, and retinal disease.

Dermatomyositis.description: An autoimmune inflammatory myopathy characterized by distinctive cutaneous findings and, in many patients, proximal muscle weakness. Adult-onset disease can be associated with an underlying malignancy.

Clinically amyopathic dermatomyositis.description: A subtype of dermatomyositis with typical skin manifestations but little or no clinically apparent muscle disease; it may still be associated with interstitial lung disease or malignancy.

Psoriasis.description: A chronic immune-mediated inflammatory skin disease causing sharply demarcated erythematous plaques with scale, commonly involving extensor surfaces.

Cutaneous lupus erythematosus.description: An autoimmune connective-tissue disorder that can cause photosensitive erythematous, scaly skin lesions and may occur with systemic lupus erythematosus.

Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease.description: A childhood osteonecrosis of the femoral capital epiphysis causing fragmentation, flattening, deformation, and possible subluxation of the femoral head; it may affect both hips.

Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia.description: An inherited skeletal dysplasia characterized by delayed, irregular, flattened, or fragmented epiphyseal ossification, commonly involving both hips and other large joints.

Developmental dysplasia of the hip with.normalized_text: Developmental dysplasia of the hip with secondary femoral head deformity
Developmental dysplasia of the hip with.description: A developmental abnormality of acetabular and femoral head coverage that can lead to hip subluxation, altered femoral head shape, and premature degenerative changes.

Gas-forming pyogenic liver abscess.description: A bacterial infection within the liver forming a pus-filled cavity; gas-producing organisms can create an air-fluid level within the abscess.

Infected hepatic cyst.description: A pre-existing simple or congenital liver cyst that becomes secondarily infected, potentially developing internal gas and an air-fluid level if infected by gas-forming bacteria or if it communicates with the biliary or gastrointestinal tract.

Subphrenic abscess.description: An infected fluid collection beneath the diaphragm, commonly occurring after abdominal infection, surgery, perforation, or trauma; it may contain gas and cause diaphragmatic elevation.

Bilateral periventricular nodular hetero.description: A neuronal migration disorder in which nodules of gray matter remain along the walls of the lateral ventricles rather than migrating normally to the cerebral cortex. It commonly presents with epilepsy and may coexist with other cortical malformations.

Bilateral perisylvian polymicrogyria.description: A malformation of cortical development characterized by excessive small, irregular cerebral gyri and abnormal cortical organization, often affecting both perisylvian regions. It can be associated with speech impairment, swallowing difficulty, epilepsy, and developmental delay.

Congenital cytomegalovirus infection wit.normalized_text: Congenital cytomegalovirus infection with cortical malformations
Congenital cytomegalovirus infection wit.description: Congenital CMV is an intrauterine viral infection that can cause ventriculomegaly, periventricular abnormalities, polymicrogyria, white-matter injury, and developmental impairment. Calcifications are often best demonstrated on CT rather than MRI.

FLNA-related periventricular nodular het.description: An inherited form of periventricular nodular heterotopia, most often related to pathogenic variants in the FLNA gene. It may be associated with bilateral ventricular-wall nodules, epilepsy, and cardiovascular or connective-tissue abnormalities.

diagnoses.name: Primary yolk sac tumor of intestine
diagnoses.normalized_text: Primary yolk sac tumor of intestine
diagnoses.icd11_title: Yolk sac tumour, unspecified site, female

Hepatoid adenocarcinoma of the jejunum (.normalized_text: Hepatoid adenocarcinoma of the jejunum (AFP-producing jejunal adenocarcinoma)
Hepatoid adenocarcinoma of the jejunum (.description: A rare, aggressive intestinal adenocarcinoma showing hepatocellular/hepatoid differentiation, often producing AFP and expressing glypican-3. It may appear as a metabolically active jejunal mass.

Enteroblastic adenocarcinoma of the smal.normalized_text: Enteroblastic adenocarcinoma of the small intestine
Enteroblastic adenocarcinoma of the smal.description: An uncommon AFP-producing adenocarcinoma with fetal-enteric/enteroblastic differentiation. Tumors may express AFP and glypican-3 and can overlap morphologically and immunohistochemically with hepatoid adenocarcinoma.

Conventional primary jejunal adenocarcin.description: A malignant epithelial tumor arising from the small-intestinal mucosa, typically forming invasive glands and potentially causing obstruction, bleeding, anemia, or abdominal pain.

Metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma invo.normalized_text: Metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma involving the jejunum
Metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma invo.description: Hepatocellular carcinoma can rarely metastasize to the gastrointestinal tract and may express AFP and glypican-3, creating a major diagnostic mimic of hepatoid adenocarcinoma.

Yolk sac tumor involving the jejunum.normalized_text: Yolk sac tumor involving the jejunum
Yolk sac tumor involving the jejunum.description: A germ-cell malignancy that frequently produces AFP and may express glypican-3 and SALL4. Primary gastrointestinal involvement is very rare and is generally considered only after excluding an intestinal hepatoid adenocarcinoma and a gonadal/extragonadal germ-cell primary.

Divertículo de Meckel sangrante con muco.normalized_text: Divertículo de Meckel sangrante con mucosa gástrica ectópica
Divertículo de Meckel sangrante con muco.description: Un divertículo ileal congénito que puede contener mucosa gástrica ectópica secretora de ácido, causando ulceración del íleon adyacente y hemorragias gastrointestinales inferiores ocultas o evidentes. Una gammagrafía de tecnecio-99m pertecnetato puede mostrar captación abdominal focal simultánea con captación gástrica.

Quiste de duplicación entérica que conti.normalized_text: Quiste de duplicación entérica que contiene mucosa gástrica ectópica
Quiste de duplicación entérica que conti.description: Una duplicación congénita del tracto gastrointestinal que puede contener mucosa gástrica ectópica. La secreción ácida puede causar ulceraciones y sangrado gastrointestinal, y la mucosa gástrica ectópica puede producir captación en una gammagrafía de tecnecio-99m pertecnetato.

Sangrado gastrointestinal del intestino.normalized_text: Sangrado gastrointestinal del intestino delgado por otra lesión, como angiodisplasia o ulceración
Sangrado gastrointestinal del intestino.description: Las lesiones o úlceras vasculares del intestino delgado pueden causar pérdida crónica de sangre gastrointestinal oculta y anemia grave por deficiencia de hierro. Estas condiciones generalmente no concentran específicamente el tecnecio-99m pertecnetato, por lo que son menos consistentes con la apariencia de la gammagrafía que el divertículo de Meckel.

diagnoses.name: Diffuse idiopathic pulmonary neuroendocrine cell hyperplasia
diagnoses.normalized_text: Diffuse idiopathic pulmonary neuroendocrine cell hyperplasia
diagnoses.icd11_title: Diffuse idiopathic pulmonary neuroendocrine cell hyperplasia

Pulmonary arteriovenous malformations (P.description: Abnormal direct vascular connections between pulmonary arteries and veins, producing enhancing rounded pulmonary vascular lesions with identifiable feeding arteries and draining veins.

Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (H.normalized_text: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT, Osler-Weber-Rendu syndrome) with pulmonary arteriovenous malformations
Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (H.description: An autosomal dominant vascular disorder characterized by telangiectasias and visceral arteriovenous malformations; pulmonary AVMs are a common thoracic manifestation and may be multiple.

Pulmonary venous varix.description: A focal dilation of a pulmonary vein that can appear as a sharply defined enhancing pulmonary nodule, usually connected to venous structures rather than showing a true arterial-to-venous shunt.

Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA; f.normalized_text: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA; formerly Wegener granulomatosis)
Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA; f.description: A necrotizing small- and medium-vessel vasculitis characterized by granulomatous inflammation, often involving the upper and lower respiratory tract and kidneys. Pulmonary nodules may cavitate.

Pulmonary tuberculosis.description: Mycobacterial infection that commonly affects the upper lobes and can produce cavitation, nodules, consolidation, and granulomatous inflammation.

Chronic cavitary pulmonary aspergillosis.description: A chronic fungal infection in which Aspergillus colonizes or invades abnormal lung tissue, producing one or more thick-walled cavities, often in the upper lobes.

Pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis.description: A smoking-associated interstitial lung disease characterized by upper- and mid-lung-predominant nodules that may evolve into irregular cysts and cavitary lesions.

Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopat.description: A demyelinating central nervous system disease caused by reactivation of JC polyomavirus, usually in patients with impaired cellular immunity such as HIV infection or immunosuppressive therapy.

HIV-associated progressive multifocal le.description: PML occurring in a person with HIV-related immune dysfunction; it is caused by JC virus reactivation in the brain and is a classic opportunistic neurologic infection.

JC virus granule cell neuronopathy.description: A less common JC virus neurologic disease involving cerebellar granule neurons, typically causing progressive cerebellar dysfunction in immunocompromised patients.

Pompe disease (glycogen storage disease.normalized_text: Pompe disease (glycogen storage disease type II)
Pompe disease (glycogen storage disease.description: An autosomal-recessive lysosomal acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency causing lysosomal glycogen accumulation, particularly in cardiac and skeletal muscle. Infantile disease commonly causes hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

Danon disease (LAMP2-related glycogen st.description: An X-linked lysosomal/autophagy disorder due to LAMP2 deficiency, causing severe hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, ventricular pre-excitation, skeletal myopathy, and sometimes intellectual disability.

PRKAG2 syndrome.description: An inherited glycogen-storage cardiomyopathy caused by pathogenic variants in PRKAG2, characterized by ventricular pre-excitation, conduction disease, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and myocardial glycogen accumulation.

Fabry disease.description: An X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by alpha-galactosidase A deficiency, leading to globotriaosylceramide accumulation and progressive cardiac, renal, neurologic, and dermatologic disease. Cardiac involvement can cause left ventricular hypertrophy.

Hydronephrosis.description: Dilation of the renal pelvis and calyces caused by impaired urine drainage; the ultrasound appearance is consistent with a dilated central collecting system.

Obstructive uropathy due to ureteral obs.normalized_text: Obstructive uropathy due to ureteral obstruction
Obstructive uropathy due to ureteral obs.description: Urinary tract obstruction, commonly from a ureteral stone, stricture, or mass, can produce upstream dilation of the kidney collecting system.

Ureteropelvic junction obstruction.description: A narrowing or functional obstruction at the junction of the renal pelvis and ureter that causes hydronephrosis, often with a dilated renal pelvis and calyces.

Vesicoureteral reflux with reflux nephro.description: Backward flow of urine from the bladder toward the kidneys can cause intermittent or persistent dilation of the renal collecting system and, over time, renal scarring.

Lepromatous leprosy.description: A multibacillary form of Hansen disease caused by Mycobacterium leprae, characterized by diffuse skin infiltration, numerous papules and nodules, facial thickening, and frequent involvement of the ears.

Disseminated cutaneous histoplasmosis.description: A systemic fungal infection caused by Histoplasma species that can produce numerous papules, nodules, pustules, ulcers, and crusted lesions on the face, particularly in immunocompromised patients.

Disseminated cutaneous cryptococcosis.description: A fungal infection caused by Cryptococcus species, usually occurring in immunocompromised individuals and often causing umbilicated papules, nodules, pustules, ulcers, or molluscum-like facial lesions.

Diffuse cutaneous leishmaniasis.description: A chronic form of leishmaniasis in which impaired cellular immunity permits widespread parasite-containing papules, nodules, plaques, and sometimes ulcerated lesions, often involving the face and ears.

Renal cell carcinoma.description: A malignant tumor arising from renal tubular cells, commonly presenting as a solid or heterogeneous enhancing renal mass with areas of necrosis or cystic degeneration.

Renal oncocytoma.description: A benign epithelial renal tumor that can appear as a well-circumscribed solid renal mass and may be difficult to distinguish from renal cell carcinoma on imaging alone.

Renal angiomyolipoma.description: A usually benign renal tumor composed of variable amounts of fat, smooth muscle, and abnormal blood vessels. Classic lesions contain macroscopic fat, although fat-poor angiomyolipomas may mimic renal cell carcinoma.

Complex renal cystic lesion (Bosniak III.normalized_text: Complex renal cystic lesion (Bosniak III or IV cystic renal mass)
Complex renal cystic lesion (Bosniak III.description: A complex renal cyst with thick walls, septations, nodular soft-tissue components, or enhancement. Higher Bosniak categories have a substantial risk of malignancy, particularly cystic renal cell carcinoma.

Sepsis capnocitophaga canimorsus fulmina.normalized_text: Sepsis capnocitophaga canimorsus fulminante con coagulación intravascular diseminada (CID) y púrpura fulminante
Sepsis capnocitophaga canimorsus fulmina.description: Una infección grave de torrente sanguíneo zoonótico causada por una varilla gram-negativa esbelta y meticulosa, comúnmente asociada a la exposición de perros o gatos. Puede causar rápidamente shock séptico, CID, fallo multiorgánico y necrosis cutánea púrpurica, especialmente en personas con asplenia, trastorno por consumo de alcohol o inmunosupresión.

Septicemia meningocócica con púrpura ful.description: Infección fulminante en sangre con Neisseria meningitidis que puede producir shock séptico rápido, CID, trombocitopenia, púrpura fulminante, lesión suprarrenal e insuficiencia multiorgánica.

Septicemia de Vibrio vulnificus.description: Una infección grave causada por una bacteria marina gram-negativa curvada, generalmente tras la ingestión de mariscos crudos o la exposición al agua de mar, especialmente en pacientes con enfermedad hepática crónica. Puede causar shock séptico, CID, lesiones cutáneas bullosas o púrpuras y fallo multiorgánico.

Sepsis neumocócica abrumadora con CID.description: Infección invasiva grave por Streptococcus pneumoniae, especialmente en pacientes asplénicos o inmunodeprimidos, que puede causar shock séptico, CIV, púrpura fulminana, lesión renal aguda y disfunción hepática.

diagnoses.name: MELAS syndrome
diagnoses.icd11_title: MELAS - [Mitochondrial encephalopathy with lactic acidosis and stroke-like episodes] syndrome

Left atrial myxoma with cardioembolic ac.normalized_text: Left atrial myxoma with cardioembolic acute ischemic stroke
Left atrial myxoma with cardioembolic ac.description: A left atrial myxoma is a benign primary cardiac tumor that can release tumor fragments or thrombus, causing systemic arterial emboli including acute cerebral infarction.

Cardioembolic left middle cerebral arter.normalized_text: Cardioembolic left middle cerebral artery ischemic stroke
Cardioembolic left middle cerebral arter.description: An acute ischemic stroke occurs when an embolus blocks a cerebral artery. Cardiac emboli may arise from atrial tumors, atrial thrombus, atrial fibrillation, valvular disease, or other intracardiac sources.

Left atrial thrombus with cerebral embol.normalized_text: Left atrial thrombus with cerebral embolization
Left atrial thrombus with cerebral embol.description: A thrombus within the left atrium or left atrial appendage can embolize into the systemic circulation and obstruct a cerebral artery, producing an acute ischemic infarct.

Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.description: A malignant epithelial tumor of the pancreatic ducts, commonly arising in the pancreatic head and causing obstruction of the distal common bile duct, jaundice, and elevated CA 19-9.

Distal extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.description: A bile-duct adenocarcinoma arising in the distal common bile duct. It often presents with painless obstructive jaundice and can be difficult to distinguish from pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

Ampullary adenocarcinoma.description: A malignant tumor arising from the ampulla of Vater, where the bile duct and pancreatic duct enter the duodenum. It commonly causes early biliary obstruction and jaundice.

Gallbladder carcinoma with biliary obstr.description: Gallbladder adenocarcinoma is a biliary tract malignancy that may invade the hepatic hilum or extrahepatic bile ducts, causing jaundice and cholestatic liver-test abnormalities.

Gallbladder torsion (gallbladder volvulu.description: A rare mechanical twisting of the gallbladder around its cystic duct and vascular pedicle, which can obstruct blood flow and cause acute ischemic cholecystitis.

Acute cholecystitis.description: Inflammation of the gallbladder, most commonly caused by obstruction of the cystic duct by a gallstone.

Cystic duct obstruction from cholelithia.description: Blockage of the cystic duct by a gallstone, which may cause biliary colic or progress to acute cholecystitis.

Juvenile osteochondritis dissecans of th.normalized_text: Juvenile osteochondritis dissecans of the medial femoral condyle
Juvenile osteochondritis dissecans of th.description: A focal osteochondral disorder in which subchondral bone and overlying cartilage of the femoral condyle become damaged; it commonly affects adolescents and often involves the lateral aspect of the medial femoral condyle.

Normal developmental irregularity of the.normalized_text: Normal developmental irregularity of the distal femoral epiphysis
Normal developmental irregularity of the.description: Children and adolescents can have benign irregular ossification of the femoral condyles that can mimic an osteochondral lesion, particularly when there is no associated clinical knee dysfunction.

Osteochondral injury or healing osteocho.normalized_text: Osteochondral injury or healing osteochondral fracture of the femoral condyle
Osteochondral injury or healing osteocho.description: An osteochondral injury involves trauma to articular cartilage and adjacent subchondral bone; radiographs may show focal irregularity, flattening, or a lucent defect in the involved condyle.

Lichen planopilaris.description: A lymphocyte-mediated inflammatory disorder of hair follicles that can cause perifollicular scaling, follicular keratotic papules, and permanent scarring alopecia.

Graham-Little-Piccardi-Lassueur syndrome.description: A rare variant of lichen planopilaris characterized by scarring scalp alopecia together with widespread follicular keratotic papules; loss of axillary or pubic hair may also occur.

Discoid lupus erythematosus of the scalp.normalized_text: Discoid lupus erythematosus of the scalp
Discoid lupus erythematosus of the scalp.description: A chronic cutaneous lupus subtype that commonly produces inflammatory plaques with follicular plugging, pigment change, and irreversible scarring alopecia.

Follicular lichen planus.description: A follicular form of lichen planus in which keratotic papules develop around hair follicles and may coexist with lichen planopilaris of the scalp.

Livedoid vasculopathy.description: A thrombotic occlusive disease of small dermal blood vessels that causes recurrent, painful ulcers around the ankles and feet and may heal with white stellate scars (atrophie blanche). Histology commonly shows hyalinized, thickened superficial dermal vessels with fibrin thrombi and relatively limited inflammation.

Cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa.description: A skin-limited necrotizing vasculitis involving small- and medium-sized arteries in the deep dermis or subcutaneous tissue. It can produce tender nodules, livedo reticularis, purpura, and painful ulcers on the lower legs and ankles.

Martorell hypertensive ischemic leg ulce.description: A painful ischemic ulcer due to hypertensive arteriolosclerosis of small cutaneous vessels, classically affecting the lateral lower leg, supramalleolar region, or Achilles-area skin in patients with longstanding hypertension and often diabetes.

Calciphylaxis (calcific uremic arteriolo.description: A severe ischemic skin disorder caused by calcification and thrombosis of small dermal and subcutaneous vessels, most often in advanced chronic kidney disease or dialysis patients. It produces exquisitely painful violaceous plaques that progress to necrotic ulcers.

Chronic venous leg ulcer with stasis der.normalized_text: Chronic venous leg ulcer with stasis dermatitis
Chronic venous leg ulcer with stasis der.description: Venous insufficiency can cause edema, brown hemosiderin pigmentation, eczematous dermatitis, and chronic ulceration, usually in the gaiter area around the medial ankle.

diagnoses.name: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
diagnoses.icd11_title: Gastrointestinal stromal tumour of unspecified gastrointestinal sites

Epithelioid angiosarcoma.description: A high-grade malignant vascular tumor composed of atypical epithelioid endothelial cells. Tumor cells may form poorly developed vascular channels and show intracytoplasmic vacuoles; endothelial immunostains such as CD31, ERG, FLI1, and CD34 are typically positive.

Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma.description: A malignant vascular neoplasm of intermediate biologic behavior, usually composed of epithelioid endothelial cells with cytoplasmic vacuoles in a myxohyaline or fibrous stroma. It generally expresses endothelial markers including CD31, ERG, FLI1, and CD34.

Epithelioid sarcoma, proximal type.description: An aggressive soft-tissue sarcoma composed of large epithelioid and rhabdoid-appearing malignant cells. It often expresses cytokeratin, EMA, and sometimes CD34, with loss of INI1/SMARCB1 in most cases.

diagnoses.name: Malignant gastrointestinal stromal tumor
diagnoses.icd11_title: Malignant GIST - [gastrointestinal stromal tumour] of large intestine

Gastric glomus tumor (large or potential.normalized_text: Gastric glomus tumor (large or potentially malignant gastric glomus tumor)
Gastric glomus tumor (large or potential.description: A rare mesenchymal tumor derived from modified smooth-muscle glomus cells, most often arising in the gastric antrum. It typically shows uniform round cells arranged around branching blood vessels and expresses smooth-muscle markers such as SMA, while CD34 may highlight the vascular network rather than tumor cells.

Gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST).description: GIST is the most common mesenchymal neoplasm of the stomach, arising from interstitial cells of Cajal. It can form a large exophytic gastric mass with hemorrhage or necrosis and usually expresses KIT (CD117) and DOG1.

Gastric leiomyoma or leiomyosarcoma.description: These are smooth-muscle tumors of the stomach. Leiomyoma is benign, whereas leiomyosarcoma is malignant and generally shows infiltrative growth, significant atypia, necrosis, and increased mitotic activity.

Gastric schwannoma.description: Gastric schwannoma is an uncommon benign peripheral-nerve-sheath tumor, usually composed of spindle cells with a peripheral lymphoid cuff and diffuse S-100/SOX10 positivity.

Epidermolytic verrucous epidermal nevus.description: A mosaic keratinization disorder presenting as localized, linear or segmental hyperkeratotic verrucous plaques. Histology shows epidermolytic hyperkeratosis with vacuolization of suprabasal keratinocytes and prominent keratohyalin granules.

Verrucous epidermal nevus.description: A benign hamartomatous proliferation of epidermis that usually presents as persistent hyperpigmented, rough, papillomatous, or verrucous plaques, often in a unilateral or linear pattern.

Epidermolytic ichthyosis with mosaic/loc.description: A keratin 1 or keratin 10 disorder characterized by epidermolytic hyperkeratosis. In mosaic forms, disease may be restricted to a localized segment of skin rather than causing generalized ichthyosis.

Extraskeletal chondrosarcoma.description: A malignant cartilage-producing tumor arising in soft tissues rather than directly from bone; it can form a large lobulated pelvic mass with chondroid calcification.

Extraskeletal mesenchymal chondrosarcoma.description: A rare aggressive subtype of extraskeletal chondrosarcoma composed of undifferentiated cells and cartilage, often presenting as a calcified soft-tissue mass.

Synovial sarcoma.description: A malignant soft-tissue sarcoma that may occur near joints or in deep pelvic soft tissues and can contain focal or extensive calcification.

Extraskeletal osteosarcoma.description: A rare high-grade malignant soft-tissue tumor that produces osteoid or bone matrix outside the skeleton, usually appearing as a mineralized soft-tissue mass.

Calcified uterine leiomyoma.description: A benign uterine smooth-muscle tumor that may undergo hyaline degeneration and dystrophic calcification, sometimes becoming a large pelvic mass.

Síndrome de persona rígida clásico (SPS).normalized_text: Síndrome de persona rígida clásico (SPS) asociado a anticuerpos anti-GAD
Síndrome de persona rígida clásico (SPS).description: Trastorno neurológico autoinmune caracterizado por rigidez muscular progresiva, espasmos dolorosos e hiperexcitabilidad del sistema motor. Frecuentemente se asocia a anticuerpos contra la descarboxilasa del ácido glutámico (anti-GAD) y actividad muscular continua en EMG.

Encefalomielitis progresiva con rigidez.normalized_text: Encefalomielitis progresiva con rigidez y mioclonías (PERM)
Encefalomielitis progresiva con rigidez.description: Forma más grave del espectro de los trastornos de rigidez muscular autoinmunes. Puede producir rigidez, espasmos, mioclonías, hiperexcitabilidad del tronco encefálico y alteraciones autonómicas; suele asociarse a anticuerpos anti-glicina, aunque también puede haber anti-GAD.

Neuromiotonía adquirida autoinmune (sínd.description: Trastorno de hiperexcitabilidad de nervios periféricos que causa actividad muscular continua, fasciculaciones, calambres, rigidez, mioquimia y relajación muscular retrasada. Puede tener una base autoinmune y responder a inmunoterapia.

Giant cell arteritis with scalp necrosis.normalized_text: Giant cell arteritis with scalp necrosis
Giant cell arteritis with scalp necrosis.description: A granulomatous vasculitis of medium and large arteries, usually affecting older adults. Involvement of superficial temporal, occipital, carotid, or subclavian branches can cause scalp ischemia and necrosis.

Takayasu arteritis.description: A chronic large-vessel vasculitis affecting the aorta and its major branches, causing stenosis, occlusion, aneurysm formation, and ischemic manifestations. Severe carotid or subclavian involvement can rarely contribute to scalp ischemia.

Atherosclerotic carotid or subclavian ar.normalized_text: Atherosclerotic carotid or subclavian artery disease causing scalp ischemia
Atherosclerotic carotid or subclavian ar.description: Atherosclerotic plaque can narrow or occlude major cervical arteries, reducing perfusion to downstream tissues. Severe multivessel disease may rarely cause ischemic scalp ulceration.

Subclavian steal syndrome due to proxima.normalized_text: Subclavian steal syndrome due to proximal subclavian artery stenosis
Subclavian steal syndrome due to proxima.description: Proximal subclavian artery stenosis can divert blood flow through the vertebral circulation toward the arm, producing vertebrobasilar or upper-extremity ischemic symptoms. It may coexist with broader cervicocranial vascular disease.

Embolic or thrombotic occlusion of scalp.normalized_text: Embolic or thrombotic occlusion of scalp arterial branches
Embolic or thrombotic occlusion of scalp.description: Acute thrombosis or embolization to branches of the external carotid circulation can cause focal scalp ischemia, ulceration, and necrosis. This may occur in the setting of proximal arterial disease or a cardiac embolic source.

Cold agglutinin disease (cold autoimmune.normalized_text: Cold agglutinin disease (cold autoimmune hemolytic anemia)
Cold agglutinin disease (cold autoimmune.description: An autoimmune hemolytic anemia in which cold-reacting antibodies, usually IgM, cause red-cell agglutination and complement-mediated hemolysis.

Warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia.description: Immune destruction of red blood cells by antibodies that react optimally at body temperature, producing anemia and hemolysis.

In vitro hemolysis of the blood specimen.normalized_text: In vitro hemolysis of the blood specimen (preanalytical sample hemolysis)
In vitro hemolysis of the blood specimen.description: Red-cell rupture occurring during or after collection, rather than necessarily in the patient, causing serum/plasma to appear orange, pink, or red.

EDTA-dependent pseudothrombocytopenia.description: A laboratory artifact in which EDTA-dependent antibodies cause platelets to aggregate in a collection tube, leading to platelet clumps on a smear and a falsely low automated platelet count.

Necrobiosis lipoidica.description: A chronic granulomatous skin disorder, often associated with diabetes mellitus, characterized by yellow-brown atrophic plaques with raised red-violaceous borders. Histology typically shows dermal collagen degeneration (necrobiotic collagen) with palisading granulomatous inflammation.

Granuloma annulare.description: A benign inflammatory skin condition causing annular papules or plaques, with histology showing palisading histiocytes surrounding altered collagen and mucin.

Rheumatoid nodule.description: A firm subcutaneous nodule associated with rheumatoid arthritis, usually over pressure points. Histology may show central fibrinoid necrosis surrounded by palisading histiocytes.

Pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1B (PHP1B).description: An inherited or epigenetic disorder of renal resistance to parathyroid hormone (PTH), most often caused by abnormal methylation at the GNAS locus. The kidneys do not appropriately respond to PTH, causing hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, and compensatory elevation of PTH despite normal kidney function.

Pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1A (PHP1A;.description: A form of PTH resistance caused by a maternally inherited inactivating GNAS mutation. It produces hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, elevated PTH, and frequently resistance to TSH and other hormones; it is often associated with Albright hereditary osteodystrophy.

Pseudohypoparathyroidism type 2 (PHP2).description: A less common form of renal PTH resistance in which PTH signaling is impaired downstream of cyclic AMP generation. It can cause hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, and elevated PTH with preserved renal function.

Chronic kidney disease with secondary hy.normalized_text: Chronic kidney disease with secondary hyperparathyroidism
Chronic kidney disease with secondary hy.description: Reduced kidney function causes phosphate retention, impaired calcitriol production, hypocalcemia, and secondary elevation of PTH. This is a common cause of the combination of low calcium, high phosphate, and high PTH.

Vitamin D deficiency or impaired vitamin.normalized_text: Vitamin D deficiency or impaired vitamin D activation
Vitamin D deficiency or impaired vitamin.description: Insufficient vitamin D reduces intestinal calcium absorption and causes secondary hyperparathyroidism. Serum phosphate is usually low or normal because elevated PTH promotes urinary phosphate loss.

Histoplasmosis diseminada.description: Infección sistémica con Histoplasma capsulatum, que a menudo afecta al sistema reticuloendotelial, hígado, bazo, médula ósea y pulmones. La enfermedad diseminada grave puede causar citopenias, hepatitis, disfunción renal, coagulopatía y linfosoistiocitosis hemofagocítica secundaria.

Linfosotiocitosis hemofagocítica secunda.description: Un síndrome hiperinflamatorio potencialmente mortal causado por una activación inmunitaria descontrolada, frecuentemente desencadenada por infecciones fúngicas diseminadas, infecciones virales, malignidades o enfermedades autoinmunes. Suele producir citopenias, disfunción hepática, hipofibrinogenemia e insuficiencia multiorgánica.

Criptococcosis diseminada.description: Una infección sistémica por hongos causada por especies de Cryptococcus, generalmente en hospedadores inmunodeprimidos. Puede afectar a los pulmones, el sistema nervioso central, el hígado, la médula ósea, los riñones y el torrente sanguíneo; la infección diseminada puede causar citopenias y disfunción hepática.

Coagulación intravascular diseminada (CI.normalized_text: Coagulación intravascular diseminada (CID) asociada a sepsis debido a una infección fúngica invasiva
Coagulación intravascular diseminada (CI.description: La CID es un trastorno sistémico adquirido de la coagulación causado por la activación descontrolada de la coagulación, comúnmente durante una infección grave. Conduce al consumo de plaquetas y factores de coagulación, elevación del D-dímero, fibrinógeno bajo, hemorragia o trombosis, y disfunción multiorgánica.

Pancreatic metastasis from clear-cell re.normalized_text: Pancreatic metastasis from clear-cell renal cell carcinoma
Pancreatic metastasis from clear-cell re.description: Metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma can involve the pancreas, often appearing as a hypervascular pancreatic mass. Histology typically shows nests of clear cells separated by delicate vascular septa, with supportive immunohistochemical staining such as PAX8, CD10, and RCC-marker positivity.

Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor.description: A pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor is a neoplasm arising from endocrine cells of the pancreas. These tumors can be hypervascular on imaging and may have nested cellular architecture; some tumors can have clear-cell cytoplasmic features.

Primary pancreatic clear-cell neoplasm.description: Rare primary pancreatic tumors, including clear-cell variants of pancreatic ductal carcinoma or other epithelial neoplasms, may contain cells with clear cytoplasm. These diagnoses require exclusion of metastatic renal cell carcinoma using immunohistochemistry and clinical imaging.

Familial syringomyelia.description: A disorder characterized by formation of a fluid-filled cavity (syrinx) within the spinal cord; the pedigree suggests a possible inherited, likely autosomal-recessive, form.

Hydromyelia.description: Abnormal dilatation of the central canal of the spinal cord by cerebrospinal fluid, sometimes considered part of the syringomyelia spectrum.

Chiari I malformation-associated syringo.description: Syringomyelia may develop when downward displacement of the cerebellar tonsils disrupts cerebrospinal-fluid flow at the foramen magnum; dedicated brain/cervicomedullary imaging is needed to confirm this cause.

Intramedullary spinal cord tumor with se.normalized_text: Intramedullary spinal cord tumor with secondary syrinx
Intramedullary spinal cord tumor with se.description: Tumors such as ependymoma or astrocytoma can obstruct cerebrospinal-fluid flow within the cord and produce a syrinx above or below the lesion.

Posterior reversible encephalopathy synd.description: A clinicoradiologic syndrome of vasogenic cerebral edema, commonly related to severe hypertension, renal failure, eclampsia, immunosuppressive drugs, or systemic illness. It typically affects posterior parieto-occipital regions and may include restricted diffusion or small hemorrhages.

Cerebral fat embolism syndrome.description: A neurologic complication of fat embolization, usually after long-bone or pelvic fractures, orthopedic surgery, or major trauma. MRI may show multiple scattered diffusion-restricted lesions and numerous petechial microhemorrhages.

Cerebral amyloid angiopathy-related infl.description: An inflammatory reaction around amyloid-laden cortical and leptomeningeal vessels, usually in older adults. MRI commonly demonstrates asymmetric patchy white-matter edema with lobar cerebral microbleeds and sometimes small ischemic lesions.

Intramedullary spinal neurosarcoidosis.description: Sarcoidosis involving the cervical spinal cord, characterized by noncaseating granulomatous inflammation and often producing enhancing intramedullary lesions with cord swelling.

Intramedullary spinal tuberculoma or tub.normalized_text: Intramedullary spinal tuberculoma or tuberculous myelitis
Intramedullary spinal tuberculoma or tub.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection involving the spinal cord, which can form granulomatous intramedullary lesions and cause myelopathy.

Fungal granulomatous myelitis.description: A fungal infection of the spinal cord, such as cryptococcosis, histoplasmosis, or coccidioidomycosis, which may produce granulomas and enhancing intramedullary lesions, especially in immunocompromised patients.

Pulmonary actinomycosis.description: A chronic suppurative bacterial infection caused by Actinomyces species, often producing mass-like consolidation, abscesses, cavitation, and fibrosis that can mimic lung cancer or tuberculosis.

Necrotizing bacterial pneumonia with pul.normalized_text: Necrotizing bacterial pneumonia with pulmonary abscess
Necrotizing bacterial pneumonia with pul.description: A severe bacterial lung infection causing parenchymal necrosis and abscesses, commonly due to anaerobes, Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, or mixed aspiration-related flora.

Pulmonary tuberculosis.description: Infection of the lungs by Mycobacterium tuberculosis that may cause consolidation, cavitation, granulomatous inflammation, and chronic pulmonary destruction.

Pulmonary aspergillosis.description: A fungal lung infection caused by Aspergillus species that can present as chronic cavitary pulmonary aspergillosis, invasive aspergillosis, or fungal colonization of pre-existing cavities.

Ascariasis (Ascaris lumbricoides infecti.description: Intestinal infection by the large roundworm Ascaris lumbricoides. Histologic cross-sections may show a thick cuticle, prominent muscle layers, pseudocoelom, and reproductive tubes containing eggs.

Toxocariasis (Toxocara species infection.description: A zoonotic nematode infection caused by dog or cat roundworms. Humans usually harbor larval forms in tissues rather than mature egg-producing adult worms.

Anisakiasis.description: Infection with larvae of Anisakis nematodes acquired from raw or undercooked marine fish or squid. Larvae can invade the stomach or intestinal wall and cause acute gastrointestinal symptoms.

Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP).description: A neurodegenerative tauopathy characterized by early postural instability, parkinsonism, cognitive/behavioral changes, and impaired vertical supranuclear eye movements. MRI may show predominant midbrain atrophy with relative pontine preservation, producing the 'hummingbird' sign.

Parkinson disease.description: A progressive synucleinopathy causing bradykinesia with resting tremor, rigidity, and postural instability. Eye movement abnormalities can occur later, but prominent early vertical supranuclear gaze palsy is unusual.

Multiple system atrophy (MSA).description: A rapidly progressive synucleinopathy characterized by autonomic failure with parkinsonism (MSA-P) and/or cerebellar ataxia (MSA-C). MRI may show pontocerebellar atrophy or the 'hot-cross-bun' sign rather than isolated midbrain atrophy.

Cryptococcosis (Cryptococcus neoformans.description: An invasive fungal infection caused by encapsulated yeast, most often Cryptococcus neoformans. It can cause pulmonary disease and disseminate to the central nervous system, producing cryptococcal meningitis.

Cryptococcosis due to Cryptococcus gatti.description: A cryptococcal infection caused by Cryptococcus gattii, an encapsulated yeast that may infect immunocompetent as well as immunocompromised individuals and can cause pulmonary cryptococcomas or central nervous system infection.

Disseminated cryptococcal infection.description: Systemic spread of Cryptococcus, usually in patients with impaired cell-mediated immunity, which can involve blood, lungs, skin, and especially the meninges.

Acute pontine ischemic infarction.description: An acute stroke involving the pons, commonly caused by occlusion of small perforating branches of the basilar artery. It typically produces restricted diffusion on diffusion-weighted MRI.

Central pontine myelinolysis (osmotic de.description: Demyelination of central pontine fibers, most often occurring after overly rapid correction of chronic hyponatremia or other major osmotic shifts. MRI may show central pontine T2 hyperintensity and diffusion restriction.

Rhombencephalitis.description: Inflammation of the brainstem and cerebellum, which may be infectious, autoimmune, or paraneoplastic. It can cause T2/FLAIR hyperintense brainstem lesions and occasionally diffusion abnormalities.

Pontine neoplasm, such as glioma.description: A primary glial tumor of the pons can produce T2 hyperintensity and enlargement or distortion of the brainstem, usually with a more chronic progressive course than stroke.

Congenital Plasmodium falciparum malaria.description: Malaria acquired transplacentally or around delivery, caused by Plasmodium falciparum. It can produce severe hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, high parasitemia with multiple intraerythrocytic ring forms, metabolic/respiratory abnormalities, and central nervous system involvement.

Congenital malaria due to Plasmodium viv.normalized_text: Congenital malaria due to Plasmodium vivax or Plasmodium ovale
Congenital malaria due to Plasmodium viv.description: Congenital infection with non-falciparum malaria parasites can cause neonatal anemia, thrombocytopenia, and parasitemia. P. vivax and P. ovale usually infect reticulocytes and tend to have lower parasite burdens than P. falciparum.

Babesiosis, including congenital babesio.description: Babesiosis is an intraerythrocytic protozoal infection, usually transmitted by ticks but rarely transmitted congenitally or by transfusion. It causes hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia; blood smears may show ring forms and, classically, Maltese-cross tetrads.

Severe malaria with cerebral involvement.description: Severe malaria is most often caused by P. falciparum and may involve extensive hemolysis, thrombocytopenia, coagulation activation, acidosis, respiratory compromise, and neurologic or cerebrospinal-fluid abnormalities.

Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (O.normalized_text: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (Osler-Weber-Rendu syndrome) with visceral arteriovenous malformations
