Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (O.description: An inherited vascular disorder characterized by telangiectasias and arteriovenous malformations (AVMs), commonly involving the lungs, liver, brain, and gastrointestinal tract.

Multiple pulmonary arteriovenous malform.description: Pulmonary AVMs are direct abnormal connections between pulmonary arteries and veins, producing rounded enhancing lung lesions with feeding and draining vessels. They may occur sporadically or in association with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia.

Metastatic malignancy involving the lung.normalized_text: Metastatic malignancy involving the lungs and liver
Metastatic malignancy involving the lung.description: Disseminated cancer can produce multiple pulmonary nodules and hepatic lesions. Common primary sites include colorectal, renal, thyroid, breast, melanoma, and neuroendocrine tumors.

Multifocal venous malformations / system.normalized_text: Multifocal venous malformations / systemic vascular malformation syndrome
Multifocal venous malformations / system.description: Venous malformations are congenital low-flow vascular lesions that may involve multiple organs and can contain phleboliths. Syndromic forms can involve visceral organs and the pelvis.

Thyrotoxic periodic paralysis.description: An acute, potentially life-threatening complication of thyrotoxicosis in which potassium shifts into cells, causing severe hypokalemia and episodic muscle weakness or paralysis.

Graves disease.description: An autoimmune cause of hyperthyroidism due to thyroid-stimulating antibodies, typically producing diffuse thyroid enlargement and marked increased gland vascularity; it can precipitate thyrotoxic periodic paralysis.

Hashimoto thyroiditis with transient thy.description: An autoimmune lymphocytic thyroiditis that usually leads to hypothyroidism but may initially cause transient hyperthyroidism from release of preformed thyroid hormone. Histology commonly shows dense lymphocytic infiltration and lymphoid follicle formation.

Torus palatinus.description: A benign developmental bony overgrowth arising from the midline hard palate, often appearing as a smooth or lobulated palatal prominence covered by normal mucosa.

Pleomorphic adenoma of a minor salivary.normalized_text: Pleomorphic adenoma of a minor salivary gland
Pleomorphic adenoma of a minor salivary.description: A common benign salivary-gland tumor that can arise from minor salivary glands of the palate and typically presents as a painless, slow-growing, firm submucosal mass.

Mucocele or mucus-retention cyst of a mi.normalized_text: Mucocele or mucus-retention cyst of a minor salivary gland
Mucocele or mucus-retention cyst of a mi.description: A benign mucus-filled lesion caused by obstruction or disruption of a salivary-gland duct; lesions are often painless and may look translucent, bluish, or normal pink depending on depth.

Palatal abscess of odontogenic origin.description: A localized collection of pus caused by infection of a maxillary tooth, which can present as a tender swelling of the palate near affected teeth.

Minor salivary-gland malignancy, such as.normalized_text: Minor salivary-gland malignancy, such as adenoid cystic carcinoma or mucoepidermoid carcinoma
Minor salivary-gland malignancy, such as.description: Malignant tumors of minor salivary glands can occur on the palate and may initially present as a firm submucosal mass; some cause pain, ulceration, numbness, or fixation as they progress.

diagnoses.name: Intervertebral disc prolapse
diagnoses.icd11_title: Intervertebral disc degeneration without prolapsed disc with determinant

L4-L5 lumbar disc herniation (central di.normalized_text: L4-L5 lumbar disc herniation (central disc extrusion/protrusion)
L4-L5 lumbar disc herniation (central di.description: Displacement of the L4-L5 intervertebral disc backward into the spinal canal, which can compress the dural sac and nearby nerve roots.

Lumbar spinal canal stenosis.description: Narrowing of the lumbar spinal canal, often caused by disc bulging/herniation and degenerative changes, with potential compression of cauda equina nerve roots.

Lumbar degenerative disc disease.description: Age- or stress-related degeneration of lumbar intervertebral discs, commonly producing disc dehydration, loss of disc height, bulging, and secondary spinal narrowing.

Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (H.normalized_text: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT, Osler-Weber-Rendu syndrome) with pulmonary and cerebral arteriovenous malformations
Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (H.description: An inherited vascular disorder characterized by abnormal direct connections between arteries and veins, commonly involving the lungs, brain, skin, and mucosal surfaces. Pulmonary arteriovenous malformations can permit paradoxical emboli to reach the brain.

Paradoxical embolic ischemic stroke caus.normalized_text: Paradoxical embolic ischemic stroke caused by a pulmonary arteriovenous malformation
Paradoxical embolic ischemic stroke caus.description: A pulmonary arteriovenous malformation creates a right-to-left shunt that bypasses the pulmonary capillary filter, allowing thrombus, septic material, or air emboli to enter the systemic circulation and cause multifocal cerebral infarction.

Cerebral arteriovenous malformation with.normalized_text: Cerebral arteriovenous malformation with hemorrhagic and ischemic complications
Cerebral arteriovenous malformation with.description: A cerebral arteriovenous malformation is an abnormal high-flow connection between cerebral arteries and veins without an intervening capillary bed. It can cause intracranial hemorrhage, seizures, headaches, focal deficits, and occasionally ischemia related to altered flow or embolic treatment complications.

Sarcoidosis.description: A systemic granulomatous inflammatory disease characterized by noncaseating granulomas, commonly involving bilateral hilar and mediastinal lymph nodes and the lungs.

Tuberculosis.description: A mycobacterial infection that can cause granulomatous lymphadenitis and pulmonary disease; granulomas are usually caseating but may occasionally appear noncaseating, particularly in early disease or limited samples.

Lymphoma.description: A malignant proliferation of lymphoid cells that commonly presents with intensely FDG-avid mediastinal lymphadenopathy; granulomatous reactions can occasionally occur adjacent to lymphoma.

Histoplasmosis or another endemic fungal.normalized_text: Histoplasmosis or another endemic fungal granulomatous infection
Histoplasmosis or another endemic fungal.description: Fungal infection, particularly histoplasmosis, can cause pulmonary and mediastinal lymph-node granulomas and may be FDG-avid on PET imaging, mimicking malignancy or sarcoidosis.

Osteopetrosis (adult-onset autosomal dom.description: An inherited disorder of impaired osteoclast-mediated bone resorption causing generalized skeletal sclerosis and markedly increased bone mineral density, although bone may remain brittle.

Skeletal fluorosis.description: A metabolic bone disease caused by chronic excessive fluoride exposure, producing osteosclerosis, increased trabecular bone, ligament calcification, and potentially bone or joint pain.

LRP5-related high bone mass syndrome.description: A genetic high-bone-mass disorder caused by increased Wnt signaling, resulting in very high bone density and generalized osteosclerosis, often with otherwise preserved health.

Sclerosteosis or van Buchem disease.description: Rare inherited sclerosing bone dysplasias caused by excessive bone formation, typically producing generalized osteosclerosis, high bone density, craniofacial overgrowth, and possible cranial-nerve compression.

Germinoma intracraneal bifocal (germinom.normalized_text: Germinoma intracraneal bifocal (germinoma supraselar y pineal)
Germinoma intracraneal bifocal (germinom.description: Un tumor de células germinales del sistema nervioso central que comúnmente afecta a las regiones pineal y supraselar. La afectación supraselar puede dañar el eje hipotalámico-hipófisis y la hipófisis posterior, causando panhipopituitarismo y diabetes insípida central. Los marcadores tumorales pueden ser normales en el germinoma puro.

Linfoma primario del sistema nervioso ce.normalized_text: Linfoma primario del sistema nervioso central que afecta a la región hipotalámica-hipofisaria
Linfoma primario del sistema nervioso ce.description: El linfoma primario del SNC es una malignidad linfoide que puede producir lesiones intracraneales que aumentan y, cuando afecta al hipotálamo, al pedúnculo hipofisario o a la región supraselar, puede causar diabetes insípida y deficiencias hormonales de la hipófisis anterior.

Neurosarcoidosis con afectación hipotalá.description: La neurosarcoidosis es una inflamación granulomatosa que afecta al sistema nervioso. La afectación del hipotálamo, el tallo hipofisario o la hipófisis puede causar diabetes insípida central, hiperprolactinemia y múltiples deficiencias hormonales anterohipófisis; también puede causar lesiones parénquimas o meníngeas que aumentan.

Histiocitosis de células de Langerhans c.normalized_text: Histiocitosis de células de Langerhans con afectación hipotalámica-hipofisaria
Histiocitosis de células de Langerhans c.description: La histiocitosis de células de Langerhans es un trastorno histiocítico clonal inflamatorio que puede infiltrarse en el tallo hipofisario y el hipotálamo. La diabetes insípida central es una manifestación endocrina frecuente, y puede aparecer disfunción hipofisaria anterior.

Hipofisitis linfocítica o infundibulo-ne.description: La inflamación autoinmune de la glándula pituitaria y el tallo puede provocar agrandamiento o engrosamiento del tallo, hiperprolactinemia, insuficiencia anterohipófisica y, a veces, diabetes insípida central cuando se ve afectada la hipófisis posterior o el infundíbulo.

Blocked premature atrial contractions (b.normalized_text: Blocked premature atrial contractions (blocked atrial bigeminy)
Blocked premature atrial contractions (b.description: Premature atrial beats occur early and may reach the atrioventricular node while it is refractory, resulting in nonconducted P waves and an apparent slow ventricular rate. This can mimic second-degree AV block.

Atrial septal aneurysm (redundant septum.normalized_text: Atrial septal aneurysm (redundant septum primum / floppy interatrial septum)
Atrial septal aneurysm (redundant septum.description: An atrial septal aneurysm is excessive mobility or bulging of the interatrial septum, often involving a redundant septum primum near the foramen ovale. It may be associated with atrial ectopy, especially in fetal or neonatal studies.

Second-degree atrioventricular block wit.description: Second-degree AV block occurs when some atrial impulses fail to conduct to the ventricles. In a 2:1 pattern, every other P wave is nonconducted, producing a slow ventricular rhythm.

Congenital complete atrioventricular blo.description: Congenital complete AV block is complete failure of atrial impulses to conduct to the ventricles, producing AV dissociation and a slow escape ventricular rhythm. It may occur in association with maternal anti-Ro/SSA antibodies or congenital heart disease.

Infantile-onset Pompe disease (acid alph.normalized_text: Infantile-onset Pompe disease (acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency, GSD type II)
Infantile-onset Pompe disease (acid alph.description: An autosomal-recessive lysosomal glycogen storage disorder caused by deficient acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA), resulting in glycogen accumulation in cardiac, skeletal, and respiratory muscle. The classic infantile form causes hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and severe muscle weakness.

Late-onset Pompe disease.description: A milder form of GAA deficiency with residual enzyme activity, usually presenting with progressive proximal skeletal-muscle and respiratory-muscle weakness rather than severe infantile cardiomyopathy.

Danon disease (LAMP2-related lysosomal g.normalized_text: Danon disease (LAMP2-related lysosomal glycogen storage cardiomyopathy)
Danon disease (LAMP2-related lysosomal g.description: An X-linked lysosomal/autophagy disorder causing hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, skeletal myopathy, and variable intellectual or developmental impairment. It can resemble Pompe disease clinically because glycogen accumulates in muscle.

Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), e.description: An aggressive non-Hodgkin B-cell lymphoma that may involve extranodal sites such as skeletal muscle, kidneys, liver, gastrointestinal tract, and bone marrow, causing anemia and elevated inflammatory markers.

Burkitt lymphoma.description: A highly aggressive mature B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma characterized by rapid proliferation, high LDH, frequent extranodal involvement, and possible bone marrow infiltration. Tumor cells commonly express CD19 and CD10.

B-cell lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma.description: A precursor B-cell malignancy involving bone marrow, blood, lymph nodes, or extranodal tissues. It commonly expresses B-cell markers including CD19 and may express CD10.

Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma.description: A rare aggressive B-cell lymphoma in which malignant lymphoid cells proliferate predominantly within small blood vessels. It can cause unexplained anemia, high LDH, inflammation, and multifocal extranodal disease without prominent lymphadenopathy.

Cellulitis of the breast.description: A bacterial infection of the skin and subcutaneous tissue causing inflammatory edema, erythema, warmth, and tenderness. Ultrasound may show diffuse skin thickening and increased echogenicity of subcutaneous fat without a drainable collection.

Mastitis.description: Inflammation of breast tissue, often infectious and commonly associated with lactation, but it can also occur in non-lactating patients. Imaging may demonstrate skin thickening, parenchymal edema, and increased vascularity.

Breast abscess.description: A localized collection of pus within breast tissue, usually developing as a complication of mastitis. Ultrasound typically demonstrates a complex fluid collection with internal debris and peripheral hyperemia.

Inflammatory breast cancer.description: An aggressive form of breast cancer in which tumor emboli obstruct dermal lymphatic vessels, producing rapid breast enlargement, erythema, edema, and skin thickening that can resemble mastitis.

Acute generalized exanthematous pustulos.description: A severe, usually medication-triggered pustular drug eruption characterized by abrupt widespread sterile pinpoint pustules on red skin, often with facial swelling.

Drug reaction with eosinophilia and syst.normalized_text: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome)
Drug reaction with eosinophilia and syst.description: A potentially serious delayed hypersensitivity reaction to a medication that commonly causes diffuse rash, facial edema, fever, blood-count abnormalities, and possible internal-organ involvement.

Generalized pustular psoriasis.description: An inflammatory psoriasis variant that produces widespread sterile pustules on inflamed skin and may be associated with systemic illness.

Morbilliform drug eruption with pustular.normalized_text: Morbilliform drug eruption with pustular features
Morbilliform drug eruption with pustular.description: A common medication-associated skin reaction causing a widespread symmetric red maculopapular rash; severe forms can include edema and pustular lesions.

Multiple keratoacanthomas (eruptive kera.description: A condition characterized by the rapid development of multiple crateriform, keratin-filled skin tumors, usually considered a variant within the squamous cell carcinoma spectrum. Lesions may arise in crops and can occur at sites of trauma.

Eruptive keratoacanthoma of Grzybowski.description: A rare form of generalized eruptive keratoacanthoma characterized by the sudden appearance of numerous small keratoacanthomas, often accompanied by marked itching and sometimes facial involvement.

Multiple self-healing squamous epithelio.description: An inherited or sporadic disorder causing recurrent crops of keratoacanthoma-like squamous tumors that typically enlarge and then regress, often leaving scars.

Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, kerat.description: A keratinocyte skin cancer that may present as a rapidly growing tender or ulcerated hyperkeratotic nodule; keratoacanthoma-type lesions can have a central keratin-filled crater and may be difficult to distinguish from keratoacanthoma histologically.

Verruca vulgaris (common warts), with po.normalized_text: Verruca vulgaris (common warts), with possible koebnerization
Verruca vulgaris (common warts), with po.description: Human papillomavirus-associated benign epidermal proliferations that produce rough, hyperkeratotic papules or plaques and can spread by autoinoculation or arise at sites of trauma.

Persistent central canal (benign central.normalized_text: Persistent central canal (benign central canal dilatation)
Persistent central canal (benign central.description: A small residual fluid-filled central canal within the spinal cord, often an incidental developmental finding and usually not associated with cord expansion or neurological symptoms.

Syringomyelia.description: A fluid-filled cavity (syrinx) within the spinal cord that may enlarge over time and can be associated with Chiari malformation, trauma, tumors, inflammation, or idiopathic causes.

Hydromyelia.description: Dilatation of the ependymal-lined central canal of the spinal cord by cerebrospinal fluid; it overlaps radiologically with syringomyelia and may be congenital or secondary to impaired CSF flow.

B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymp.normalized_text: B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with IGH-associated IRS4 rearrangement
B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymp.description: A precursor B-cell neoplasm characterized by marrow replacement by lymphoblasts. The images show blast-rich marrow and a complex translocation involving Xq22.3/IRS4 and chromosome 14, consistent with an IGH-associated IRS4 rearrangement.

B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymp.normalized_text: B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with complex cytogenetic abnormalities
B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymp.description: An aggressive hematologic malignancy of immature B-cell precursors that commonly presents with marrow and peripheral-blood blasts. Complex rearrangements involving chromosome 14 may occur and can define a molecular subtype.

Acute myeloid leukemia.description: A clonal malignancy of myeloid precursors causing accumulation of myeloblasts in marrow and often peripheral blood. It is an important morphologic differential diagnosis for acute leukemia but is less supported by the chromosome 14/IGH-associated rearrangement.

T-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma.description: A neoplasm of immature T-cell precursors that may produce marrow and peripheral-blood lymphoblasts. It can resemble B-ALL morphologically but usually has T-cell immunophenotypic features and different recurrent genetic abnormalities.

Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH).description: A life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome caused by uncontrolled activation of macrophages and lymphocytes, leading to cytokine storm, hemophagocytosis, cytopenias, liver/spleen enlargement, coagulopathy, and extremely high ferritin.

Secondary infection-associated hemophago.description: HLH triggered by a severe infection, commonly viral infections such as Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, influenza, or COVID-19, but also bacterial, fungal, or parasitic infections. It presents with the same hyperinflammatory and hematologic features as HLH.

Macrophage activation syndrome (MAS).description: A form of secondary HLH that most often complicates systemic autoimmune or autoinflammatory diseases, especially systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis, adult-onset Still disease, or systemic lupus erythematosus.

Severe sepsis with disseminated intravas.normalized_text: Severe sepsis with disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC)
Severe sepsis with disseminated intravas.description: Severe systemic infection can cause multiorgan inflammation, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia or leukocytosis, anemia, low fibrinogen, and diffuse pulmonary infiltrates. Severe sepsis may overlap with or trigger secondary HLH.

Intracranial dural arteriovenous fistula.normalized_text: Intracranial dural arteriovenous fistula (DAVF) with cortical venous reflux
Intracranial dural arteriovenous fistula.description: An abnormal acquired connection between dural arteries and dural venous sinuses or cortical veins. Cortical venous reflux can cause venous hypertension, dilated cortical veins, edema, ischemic injury, and hemorrhage.

Cerebral venous thrombosis, including is.normalized_text: Cerebral venous thrombosis, including isolated cortical vein thrombosis
Cerebral venous thrombosis, including is.description: Thrombosis of cerebral dural sinuses or cortical veins impairs venous drainage and can produce engorged veins, venous edema, venous infarction, and hemorrhage.

Cerebral arteriovenous malformation (AVM.description: A congenital vascular malformation consisting of abnormal direct arterial-to-venous connections, typically forming a nidus with enlarged feeding arteries and draining veins.

IgA vasculitis (Henoch-Schönlein purpura.description: An immune-complex small-vessel vasculitis characterized by IgA deposition in vessel walls, commonly causing palpable purpura on the lower extremities and sometimes renal, gastrointestinal, or joint involvement.

Cocaine-associated IgA vasculitis.description: A drug-associated immune-complex vasculitis, often related to cocaine exposure and sometimes levamisole adulteration, which may produce lower-extremity purpura with IgA-positive leukocytoclastic vasculitis and destructive nasal injury from intranasal cocaine use.

Granulomatosis with polyangiitis.description: An ANCA-associated necrotizing vasculitis that commonly affects the upper airways, lungs, kidneys, and skin. It can cause nasal septal destruction and purpuric skin lesions.

Levamisole-adulterated cocaine vasculopa.description: A cocaine-related autoimmune vasculopathy, often caused by levamisole contamination, producing purpuric or retiform skin lesions and sometimes neutropenia or ANCA positivity. Nasal injury may coexist because of intranasal cocaine use.

Oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma wi.normalized_text: Oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma with cervical lymph-node metastasis
Oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma wi.description: A malignant tumor arising in the oropharynx, commonly the palatine tonsil or base of tongue, often spreading to upper cervical lymph nodes. HPV-associated tumors may present primarily as a neck mass.

HPV-associated tonsillar squamous cell c.normalized_text: HPV-associated tonsillar squamous cell carcinoma with cystic nodal metastasis
HPV-associated tonsillar squamous cell c.description: Human papillomavirus-associated squamous cell carcinoma commonly develops in the tonsil or base of tongue and can produce rounded, partially cystic cervical nodal metastases, sometimes with little local throat symptomatology.

Cervical lymphoma.description: Lymphoma is a malignancy of lymphocytes that may cause enlarged cervical lymph nodes and FDG uptake on PET imaging; extranodal involvement of Waldeyer ring, including the tonsils, can occur.

Metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma t.normalized_text: Metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma to a cervical lymph node
Metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma t.description: Papillary thyroid carcinoma can metastasize to cervical lymph nodes, which may appear rounded, hypoechoic, cystic, or calcified and may demonstrate FDG uptake in more aggressive disease.

Nested variant urothelial carcinoma of t.normalized_text: Nested variant urothelial carcinoma of the urinary bladder
Nested variant urothelial carcinoma of t.description: A rare, deceptively bland-appearing variant of invasive urothelial carcinoma characterized by small irregular nests of urothelial cells infiltrating the bladder wall. It may resemble benign von Brunn nests or inverted papilloma but commonly demonstrates malignant cytogenetic abnormalities.

Conventional invasive urothelial carcino.normalized_text: Conventional invasive urothelial carcinoma of the urinary bladder
Conventional invasive urothelial carcino.description: The most common bladder malignancy, arising from urothelial lining cells and capable of invading the lamina propria and muscular bladder wall. It may show papillary, flat, nested, or solid growth patterns.

Inverted urothelial papilloma.description: A benign urothelial tumor, usually occurring in the bladder neck or trigone, with an endophytic or inverted growth pattern of urothelial nests. It can mimic nested urothelial carcinoma microscopically but generally lacks destructive invasion and malignant chromosomal abnormalities.

Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease.description: Childhood idiopathic osteonecrosis of the femoral head epiphysis, causing collapse, fragmentation, flattening, and later deformity of the femoral heads.

Bilateral avascular necrosis of the femo.normalized_text: Bilateral avascular necrosis of the femoral heads
Bilateral avascular necrosis of the femo.description: Loss of blood supply to the femoral heads leading to bone death, subchondral collapse, flattening, secondary osteoarthritis, and hip deformity.

Developmental dysplasia of the hip with.normalized_text: Developmental dysplasia of the hip with secondary degenerative arthropathy
Developmental dysplasia of the hip with.description: Abnormal development of the acetabulum and femoral head can produce chronic hip instability, deformity, subluxation, and premature osteoarthritic remodeling.

Patellar tendon rupture.description: Disruption of the patellar tendon, usually after trauma or forceful quadriceps contraction, causing upward displacement of the patella (patella alta).

Patellar tendon insufficiency or chronic.normalized_text: Patellar tendon insufficiency or chronic patellar tendon tear
Patellar tendon insufficiency or chronic.description: Partial or chronic degeneration/tearing of the patellar tendon can lengthen or weaken the extensor mechanism and produce patella alta.

Patellar instability with patella alta.description: A high-riding patella is an anatomic risk factor for recurrent lateral patellar subluxation or dislocation because the patella engages the trochlear groove later during knee flexion.

Solid pseudopapillary neoplasm of the pa.normalized_text: Solid pseudopapillary neoplasm of the pancreas
Solid pseudopapillary neoplasm of the pa.description: A rare, usually low-grade malignant pancreatic tumor that commonly occurs in young women and is characterized by solid and pseudopapillary histology, often with nuclear beta-catenin pathway marker expression.

Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor.description: A pancreatic neoplasm derived from neuroendocrine cells that may be functioning or nonfunctioning and often appears as a well-defined, hypervascular pancreatic mass.

Pancreatic acinar cell carcinoma.description: A rare malignant epithelial pancreatic tumor showing acinar differentiation; it may form a large, relatively circumscribed solid pancreatic mass.

Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.description: The most common pancreatic malignancy, usually an infiltrative duct-forming adenocarcinoma arising in the pancreatic head and often associated with biliary or pancreatic duct obstruction.

Intramuscular venous malformation (intra.normalized_text: Intramuscular venous malformation (intramuscular hemangioma) with phleboliths
Intramuscular venous malformation (intra.description: A benign low-flow vascular malformation within muscle or subcutaneous tissue. It can produce a palpable mass, superficial bluish discoloration, and multiple rounded calcified phleboliths on CT. Some lesions demonstrate FDG uptake on PET.

Intramuscular hemangioma.description: A benign vascular tumor or vascular lesion arising in skeletal muscle, often presenting as a slowly enlarging soft-tissue mass. Imaging may show vascular channels, enhancement, and phlebolith calcifications.

Soft-tissue sarcoma with dystrophic calc.description: A malignant mesenchymal tumor of soft tissues that may present as a deep enlarging mass and can occasionally contain calcification or demonstrate FDG uptake. Examples include synovial sarcoma or extraskeletal osteosarcoma.

Knee osteoarthritis (degenerative joint.description: Progressive degeneration of articular cartilage with joint-space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, and marginal osteophyte formation. The radiographs suggest degenerative changes involving the knee, including the tibiofemoral and possibly patellofemoral compartments.

Post-traumatic osteoarthritis of the kne.description: Degenerative arthritis that develops after a prior knee injury, especially an intra-articular fracture, ligament injury, or meniscal injury. It may cause uneven joint degeneration and articular surface irregularity.

Tibial plateau insufficiency fracture or.normalized_text: Tibial plateau insufficiency fracture or healed tibial plateau fracture
Tibial plateau insufficiency fracture or.description: A fracture involving the upper tibia may produce subtle depression, contour irregularity, sclerosis, or later degenerative change in the knee joint. Insufficiency fractures can occur in osteoporotic bone without major trauma.

Leiomyosarcoma.description: A malignant smooth-muscle tumor composed of atypical spindle cells, often arranged in intersecting fascicles and typically expressing smooth-muscle immunohistochemical markers such as smooth-muscle actin and desmin.

Leiomyoma.description: A benign smooth-muscle tumor that is usually well circumscribed and composed of bland spindle cells in whorled fascicles, with positivity for smooth-muscle markers.

Myofibroblastic sarcoma.description: A malignant tumor of myofibroblasts that can consist of infiltrative spindle cells and may express smooth-muscle actin, but usually has less complete smooth-muscle differentiation than leiomyosarcoma.

SHORT syndrome.description: A rare autosomal-dominant disorder, usually caused by PIK3R1 variants, characterized by short stature, partial lipodystrophy, characteristic progeroid facial appearance, delayed dentition, and insulin resistance.

Russell-Silver syndrome.description: A growth disorder characterized by prenatal and postnatal growth restriction, low weight, relative macrocephaly or prominent forehead, triangular face, feeding difficulties, and delayed bone age.

Wiedemann-Rautenstrauch syndrome.description: A rare neonatal progeroid syndrome involving growth failure, low body fat, wrinkled or aged-appearing skin, characteristic facial features, sparse scalp hair, and delayed or abnormal dentition.

Congenital generalized lipodystrophy (Be.description: A genetic disorder with near-complete absence of adipose tissue from infancy, resulting in a lean muscular appearance, visible veins, metabolic complications such as insulin resistance, hypertriglyceridemia, and fatty liver disease.
